findings.claim: the retro is the designated Adaptation event of the Sprint cycle
findings.failure_mode: role attributed to the Guide that it does not assign
findings.evidence: Deep ref L35: 'Scrum combines four formal events for inspection and adaptation'; L100: 'Each event in Scrum is a formal opportunity to inspect and adapt'. L159: the Retrospective itself inspects. The Guide designates no single Adaptation event.
findings.fix: correct: the retro is the Sprint's inspect-and-adapt event for the team's own way of working

findings.claim: specifies the output discipline (most impactful improvements addressed as soon as possible, added to the Sprint Backlog)
findings.failure_mode: optional provision stated as a rule
findings.evidence: Deep ref L161: 'The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible. They may even be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint'. Sprint Backlog placement is permitted, not required.
findings.fix: correct: (most impactful improvements addressed as soon as possible; they "may even be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint" [V])

findings.claim: The framework-immutability claim also scales directly to retro discipline: running a partial retro, one that skips data gathering, or skips the close, or produces no owned experiment, is not a retro.
findings.failure_mode: source rule applied to elements the source does not define
findings.evidence: Deep ref L13, L251: immutability covers Scrum's defined elements ('While implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, the result is not Scrum'). The Guide defines no data-gathering or close phase for the Retrospective (L157-163); those come from the Derby-Larsen agenda in the Field Guide.
findings.fix: correct: By analogy with the Guide's immutability claim, a retro that skips data gathering, skips the close, or produces no owned experiment is a partial retro. (The phases are the Field Guide's Derby-Larsen agenda; the Guide itself leaves retro structure open.)

findings.claim: The retro IS the Adaptation pillar made concrete. The Sprint Retrospective is the designated Adaptation event of the Sprint cycle.
findings.failure_mode: role attributed to the Guide that it does not assign
findings.evidence: Deep ref L35, L100, L159 as for D001.
findings.fix: correct: The retro is where the Sprint's adaptation of the team's own way of working happens. The Sprint Retrospective is one of the four inspect-and-adapt events inside the Sprint, the one aimed at quality and effectiveness.

findings.claim: Adding the improvement to the Sprint Backlog is the Guide's named mechanism for making the commitment visible and trackable.
findings.failure_mode: optional provision stated as the named mechanism
findings.evidence: Deep ref L161: improvements 'may even be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint'. The Guide names this as a possibility and gives no 'visible and trackable' rationale for it; the Sprint Backlog's visibility is stated separately (L196).
findings.fix: correct: The Guide allows improvements to be added to the Sprint Backlog for the next Sprint; doing so puts the change inside "a highly visible, real-time picture of the work" [V] the Developers inspect daily.

findings.claim: Framework immutability: partial retro is not a retro ... A retro that skips data gathering, or closes without a commitment, is a debrief, not a retro.
findings.failure_mode: source rule applied to elements the source does not define
findings.evidence: Deep ref L13, L251 (immutability of Scrum's defined elements); L157-163 (no data-gathering phase defined for the Retrospective).
findings.fix: correct: Framework immutability, by analogy. The Guide's rule is that partial Scrum is not Scrum; applied to the retro's own facilitation structure, a retro that skips data gathering or closes without a commitment is a debrief.

findings.claim: "The Sprint Retrospective concludes the Sprint. It is timeboxed to a maximum of three hours for a one-month Sprint. For shorter Sprints, the event is usually shorter."
findings.evidence: Deep ref L163 carries this as [V]; the source matches (source L518). Without the marker the protocol reads quoted text as the distillation's own wording.

findings.claim: Has at least one specific improvement been committed, registered in the Sprint Backlog, and owned? If not, the retro has produced inspection without adaptation, pointless.
findings.failure_mode: optional provision made the test for the Guide's 'pointless' verdict
findings.evidence: Deep ref L161: Sprint Backlog placement is 'may even'. The Guide's 'Inspection without adaptation is considered pointless' (L39) does not turn on Sprint Backlog registration or a named owner.
findings.fix: correct: Has at least one specific improvement been committed (ideally added to the Sprint Backlog, which the Guide allows)? If no change is committed, the retro has produced inspection without adaptation.

findings.failure_mode: role attributed to the Guide that it does not assign
findings.evidence: Deep ref L35, L100 as for D001.
findings.fix: correct: a retro (the Sprint's inspect-and-adapt event for the team's way of working)

findings.claim: The retro is the designated Adaptation event of the Sprint cycle, not a recap session. If it produces no adaptation, it has not run.
findings.failure_mode: role attributed to the Guide that it does not assign
findings.evidence: Deep ref L35, L100 as for D001; L161 gives the purpose as planning ways to increase quality and effectiveness.
findings.fix: correct: The retro's purpose is "to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness" [V], not to recap. If it produces no adaptation, it has not done its job.

findings.claim: The Guide is explicit: the most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible, not the most comfortable ones.
findings.evidence: Deep ref L161: 'The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible'. The contrast with comfortable options is not in the Guide.
findings.fix: correct: The Guide is explicit that "The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible" [V]; picking the comfortable one instead is the anti-pattern.

findings.claim: The Field Guide's 5-segment Derby-Larsen retro structure is the host methodology
findings.failure_mode: count does not match the other source's deep ref
findings.evidence: approach-perfect-field-guide-scrum-events-deep.md L216: 'Six named segments totalling 90 minutes', described as a sample agenda derived from Derby and Larsen (L242, L328).
findings.fix: correct: The Field Guide's six-segment sample agenda (derived from Derby and Larsen) is the host methodology

findings.claim: both insist the session is not a grading exercise
findings.failure_mode: position attributed to this source that it does not take
findings.evidence: TC 25-20 deep L15, L121: 'An AAR does not grade success or failure'. The Scrum Guide deep ref and source say nothing about grading.
findings.fix: correct: TC 25-20 insists the session 'does not grade success or failure' [V]; the Scrum Guide is silent on grading.

findings.claim: The Scrum Guide does not cite Agile, the Agile Manifesto, ... in its body [BT].
findings.evidence: [BT] marks the source relaying someone else. This sentence is an absence claim about citation (deep ref L247) and relays no one.

findings.claim: The empirical-pillars framing (Transparency, Inspection, Adaptation) draws on Schwaber and Sutherland's prior work but those works are not cited in the Guide itself.
findings.failure_mode: supported by the converted source but not carried by the deep ref
findings.evidence: Deep ref L243-247 names only the 1995 OOPSLA co-presentation and states no prior-work lineage. Source L656-661: the 1995 presentation 'essentially documented the learning that Ken and Jeff gained over the previous few years'; 'The Scrum Guide documents Scrum as developed, evolved, and sustained for 30-plus years by Jeff Sutherland and Ken Schwaber'.
findings.fix: cycle-to-deep: add to 'Connections the author makes in the text': "It essentially documented the learning that Ken and Jeff gained over the previous few years and made public the first formal definition of Scrum" and "The Scrum Guide documents Scrum as developed, evolved, and sustained for 30-plus years by Jeff Sutherland and Ken Schwaber" [V] (End Note, "Scrum Guide History")

findings.claim: The flat-epistemic-authority claim ("no sub-teams or hierarchies" [V]) echoes sociocratic and self-organisation traditions, none of which the Guide names [BT].
findings.failure_mode: intellectual lineage from outside the source, with a wrong marker
findings.evidence: Neither the deep ref nor the source mentions sociocracy or self-organisation traditions; the lineage is the distillation's training-data knowledge. [BT] is also wrong: the Guide relays no one here.

findings.claim: The Guide also does not address what to do when adaptation authority is absent (when the team has identified the needed change but lacks the power to make it)
findings.evidence: Deep ref L92-94: the Scrum Master serves the team by 'Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress' and the organisation by 'Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams'. The Guide gives no retro-specific escalation procedure, but it does assign the problem.
findings.fix: correct: The Guide gives no retro-specific escalation procedure when the team lacks the power to make a needed change; it assigns the problem to the Scrum Master, who is accountable for "Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress" [V].

notes: All other [V] quotations match the converted source word for word. Counts (five inspection domains) hold. Integration rows checked: TC 25-20 discovery-over-critique and open question forms (tc deep L15, L143) hold except the grading claim (D013); SSDL archetypes (brief 1.07) hold; OPL Retrospectives and Design of Experiments practices (OPL deep L213, L230) hold; Open Kanban learn-and-improve practice with Kaizen Groups and the Holistic/Systemic value (open-kanban deep L50-52, L134) hold; Org Topologies row is loose but not contradicted. The psychological-safety reading of the Transparency pillar (L26, L46, L84, L95, L104, L120) is the distillation's gloss, reasonable via the Openness value, and was graded as applied guidance. The closing claim at L143 that 'No claims in this distillation go beyond what the deep ref carries' is false until D001-D017 are fixed. Dominant pattern: the retro is repeatedly called 'the designated Adaptation event' (D001, D004, D009, D010) and Sprint Backlog registration is treated as mandatory (D002, D005, D008), where the Guide says 'may even'.
